page: Amazon Web Services r8gd.16xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features 64 dedicated physical cores on the ARMv9-based AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 CPU architecture, operating at a clock speed of 2.8 GHz. The processor includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of L3 cache, with hardware-accelerated AES cryptography. The instance is equipped with 512.0 GB of memory, yielding 8.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is bundled as a 3800 GB NVMe SSD instance store volume, and the baseline network bandwidth is rated at 30 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier memory performance, with uncached read-only memory bandwidth reaching 464.12 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 215.66 GB/sec. Multi-core CPU performance is strong, as demonstrated by a Geekbench multi-core score of 25367.0 and a Passmark physics test score of 15962.8, both placing in the top tier. Database operations and in-memory key-value performance are highly efficient, with Passmark database operations and Redis SET operations at 134.09 million operations per second scoring in the top tier. However, single-threaded performance is more moderate, with stress-ng single-core and gzip compression benchmarks falling in the average tier. LLM text generation performance varies, showing weak results for small models but top-tier efficiency for medium 7B models.

The r8gd.16xlarge offers high qualitative cost efficiency for memory-intensive and storage-heavy workloads due to its dense 512.0 GB RAM configuration and integrated 3800 GB NVMe SSD. The combination of dedicated ARM64 cores and high-speed local storage minimizes the need for external network-attached storage, optimizing resource density. This hardware profile is highly suited for high-throughput database operations, in-memory caching layers like Redis, software compilation, and static web serving.
